sentences.text: Vivek Urf Khalihar Gaur vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023

Author: Siddharth
Bench: Siddharth
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
 Reserved On:- 14.02.2023 
 Delivered On:- 21.02.2023 
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 38092 of 2022 
Applicant :- Vivek Urf Khalihar Gaur

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. 
Counsel for Applicant :- Rajiv Kumar,Ashok Kumar Upadhyay,Manoj Kumar Dubey,Vipul Kumar 
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Rajendra Prasad,Vinod Singh
Hon'ble Siddharth, J.
1.

Heard Shri Ashok Kumar Upadhyay, learned counsel for applicant; Shri Vinod Singh, learned
counsel for informant and learned Aga for State.
2.  There is allegation in the FIR that sister of the informant was studying in a college.
About one month ago, the applicant and co-accused, Suryabhan Yadav, went to her college and informed that her mother has sent them to bring her back since money is to be withdrawn from the bank.
They were having namkeen in their hands which they gave her and thereafter they took her photograph and made it viral.
Being perturbed by her photograph becoming viral and on account of shame she jumped before the train and committed suicide.

The deceased has left behind a suicide note wherein she has made allegation against co-accused, Suryabhan Yadav, that he has taken her obscene photographs and made it viral on the mobile phone of her brother.

He has submitted that subsequently the applicant has been implicated by mother of the deceased but the main allegation is against co-accused, Suryabhan Yadav, and not against the applicant.
3. Counsel for the applicant has submitted that bail application of co-accused, Suryabhan Yadav, has already been rejected by this Court vide Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 44919 of 2022 but the Vivek Urf Khalihar Gaur vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140741445/

sentences.text: 1 case of the applicant is different.

4. Learned A.G.A and learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the bail application and has stated that there is already direction of this Court in the bail rejection of the co-accused to conclude the trial on day to day basis.
The allegations against the applicant are serious.

5. Keeping in view the role of the applicant, which is different from co-accused, Suryabhan Yadav,
applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.

6. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused; submissions of the learned counsel for the parties noted above; finding force in the submissions made by the learned counsel for the applicant; keeping view the uncertainty regarding conclusion of trial; one sided investigation by police, ignoring the case of accused side; applicants being under-trial having fundamental right to speedy trial; larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India;
considering the dictum of Apex Court in the case of Satendra Kumar Antil vs. C.B.I., passed in S.L.P (Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021; considering 5-6 times overcrowding in jails over and above their capacity by the under trials and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicants have made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant, Vivek Urf Khalihar Gaur, involved in Case Crime No. 103 of 2022, under Sections- 306, 376, 328, 120-B IPC and 67, 67-A I.T. Act, Police Station- Rani Ki Sarai, District- Azamgarh, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or threaten the witnesses.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(iii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or as directed by the Court.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) In case the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence, proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicants fail to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation then the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him in accordance with law under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

sentences.text: (v) The applicant shall remain present in person before the Trial Court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
In case, of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
In case the trial has commenced, the trial court will conclude the same within a period of one year as per Section 309 Cr.P.C from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
